source.title: Superior generalization of smaller models in the presence of significant label noise
source.authors: Yihao Xue; Kyle Whitecross; Baharan Mirzasoleiman

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how model width and density affect test loss in noisy-label regression and image-classification settings, extending model-size generalization questions to different modalities and training regimes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own risk and test-loss outcomes across width and density sweeps, including explicit non-monotonic curves. It does not fit language-model scaling laws or report parameter, token, or compute exponents. Cited scaling-related findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It sweeps width or density at fixed, often small, training sets with injected label noise, in random-feature regression and supervised image classifiers. It fits no power law, varies no tokens or compute, and studies no language-model pretraining. Its question is double descent and a 'final ascent' under label noise. That is a related construct: non-monotonic loss in a data-limited, noisy-label regime. It is not a test of power-law scaling, extrapolation, allocation, shape-insensitivity or downstream predictability. The reader's T3 and its V4/V5/V7 links overreach. Density (random weight masking) at fixed parameter count is sparsity, not the depth/width shape V4 names. The non-monotonic curves come from fixed-data regimes where data is the bottleneck, which V1 and V5 exclude.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that label noise, at a large enough noise-to-sample-size ratio, causes a final ascent in test loss versus width and density. They attribute it to a variance shape change. Stronger ℓ2 regularization and robust methods (ELR, DivideMix) exacerbate it, and larger samples alleviate it. Wider but sparser models generalize better under noise.
record.recipe_differences: Studies noisy-label regression and image classification with width and density sweeps, rather than fitting language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curve shape changes with label-noise level and type, regularization strength, sample size, and density.

fits_no_version.finding: Under label noise and a sufficiently large noise-to-sample-size ratio, test loss vs width or density shows a final ascent: optimum at intermediate size. This is shown in random-feature theory and in MNIST/CIFAR/Cars experiments. Stronger ℓ2 regularization, robust methods, asymmetric noise and smaller samples make it worse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed training-set size with label noise, test loss can rise with model width or density beyond an intermediate size, rather than falling monotonically.

record.problems: The evidence concerns noisy-label regression and image classification, not language-model pretraining. The paper does not fit power laws or test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation. Many curve outcomes are described qualitatively, with no uncertainty estimates stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Additional width, density, and robust-method results appear in Figures 11–12 and 20–32. They were left out where they repeated the same qualitative findings or concerned robustness-method comparisons without adding a distinct condition needed for the versions tested.

untested.parts: All: no language-model pretraining loss, no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no extrapolation from fitted laws.
All: no depth/width shape comparison at fixed parameter count. Density masking is a different manipulation.
All: no power-law form fitted in image or other regimes. Width sweeps are at fixed small data with label noise.
All: no fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits are compared across setups.

record.verdict_notes: None of the versions is tested. The record's labels (V4 limits_scope, V5 challenges, V7 supports) are removed. The paper's regime is data-limited and noisy-label supervised classification, never framed against power-law scaling laws. Treating its non-monotonic curves as evidence against V5 or for V7 would misread it.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation from small language-model runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation, including how either scales with compute.
The paper studies width and density at fixed parameter count in a theoretical setting, but does not compare depth or a broad range of architecture details in language models.
Tests width or density sweeps in noisy-label regression and image-classification settings, but does not fit power laws; does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Predictability of downstream language-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.

Tests changes in loss-curve shape with noise, regularization, sample size, and density, but not fitted scaling exponents, compute-optimal allocation, or disagreements between published language-model fits.

rows.subject: random-feature linear network, fixed γα
rows.operation_detail: Varied width while adjusting density to keep γα fixed; measured theoretical risk.
rows.value: The text reports that test loss decreases with width.
rows.note: The result concerns width-density trade-offs at fixed parameter count in the theoretical model; no loss magnitudes are stated to assess whether changes are slight.
rows.check: Theoretical random-feature model at fixed width×density, not language-model shape (depth/width) at fixed parameters. No power-law fit. Bears on no version.

rows.subject: random-feature linear network, fixed γα
rows.operation_detail: Varied width while adjusting density to keep γα fixed; measured theoretical risk.
rows.value: The text reports U-shaped or increasing risk curves.
rows.note: The curve shape changes with width at fixed parameter count, but the text does not give numerical loss differences.
rows.check: Same as r1. The U-shaped risk under noise (κ=0.64) concerns a density-width trade-off in a toy model, not V4's architecture-shape claim.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (MNIST)
rows.stage_stated: trained on MNIST with noisy labels
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden-layer width and measured test loss.
rows.value: The loss curve develops a final ascent once noise is sufficiently high.
rows.note: The authors describe a transition from double descent or monotonic decrease to a curve with a final ascent; no fitted power law is reported.
rows.check: MNIST two-layer net with fixed data and label noise. Non-monotonic width curve, no power-law fit. Data-bottlenecked regime outside V1/V5/V7 as stated.
